statement:
For a probability $p \in (0, 1)$, the log-odds (or logit function) is defined as the natural logarithm of the odds $\frac{p}{1-p}$:
$$\operatorname{logit}(p) = \ln\left(\frac{p}{1-p}\right)$$

symbols.meaning: logit or log-odds of probability p

properties.why: Alternative algebraic and inverse hyperbolic representations of the logarithm of odds
The inverse of the logit function is the standard logistic function
The difference between the logits of two probabilities is the logarithm of the odds ratio R
Taylor series expansion of the logit function
The logit is the quantile function (inverse CDF) of the standard logistic distribution \sigma(x) = 1 / (1 + e^{-x})
Maps probability values from the open unit interval onto the entire real line

assumptions.breaks_when: p \le 0 or p \ge 1, where odds are non-positive or undefined, causing the real logarithm to be undefined
The base is less than or equal to 0 or equal to 1

failure_modes.mode: Boundary probability evaluation at p = 0 or p = 1
failure_modes.signature: Division by zero or evaluation of ln(0), yielding -\infty as p \to 0^+ and +\infty as p \to 1^-
failure_modes.cause: The odds p/(1-p) tend to 0 as p approaches 0 and diverge to infinity as p approaches 1, falling outside the open interval domain (0, 1)

failure_modes.mode: Out-of-domain evaluation for p < 0 or p > 1
failure_modes.signature: Negative argument to the logarithm function, yielding undefined real values or complex numbers
failure_modes.cause: Inputs outside [0, 1] do not represent valid probabilities and yield negative values for the odds ratio p/(1-p)

instantiation.why_here: In agrios_ws, the obstaclelayer component relies on the log-odds representation to update and track occupancy probabilities from incoming sensor measurements. Transforming probabilities into log-odds allows the component's occupancy grid algorithm to perform Bayesian updates through simple addition rather than multiplication.

The odds of occupancy for a grid cell in the obstaclelayer [scalar]
The log-odds value used by the obstaclelayer algorithm to update cell occupancy states [scalar]
